title: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and dyspepsia in adults: investigation and management
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
journal: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, clinical guideline CG184; published 3 September 2014, last updated 18 October 2019
result: Offer simple lifestyle advice including healthy eating, weight reduction and smoking cessation; raising the head of the bed and having the main meal well before bedtime may help some people [2004]. Offer full-dose PPI for 4 weeks for uninvestigated dyspepsia and for 4 or 8 weeks for GORD [2004]; if symptoms recur, the lowest effective dose and as-needed use [2004, amended 2014]; full-dose PPI for 8 weeks to heal severe oesophagitis and long-term as maintenance [new 2014]; people who had dilatation of an oesophageal stricture remain on long-term full-dose PPI. Offer an annual review to people needing long-term management and encourage stepping down or stopping treatment unless an underlying condition or comedication requires it, with return to antacid or alginate self-treatment where appropriate [2004, amended 2014]. Leave a 2-week washout after PPI use before Helicobacter pylori breath or stool testing.
